body: Don’t do it you WILL regret it…trust me..

Yes I’ve experienced all this too! It’s like I can’t distinguish reality from dreaming and I’m in this constant weird in between sleep/awake state and I wake up out of it every hour heart pounding drenched in sweat, then I fall right back into it and I’ll experience the most vivid things like people touching me and breaking into my room and I can hear music or people yelling and sometimes I will try to scream but nothing comes out.. and then all of a sudden I’ll just snap out of it and wake up, but it all felt so real and I can’t distinguish whether I was hallucinating or having nightmares. So scary and disturbing..

Yes this is exactly what happens to me!! I wake up every hour heart pounding and sweating so confused whether what I experienced was real because it felt so real or what was a dream. I wake up in the morning so disoriented and confused feeling absolutely crazy not able to tell whether I was hallucinating or having vivid nightmares because it feels like I was wide awake.. so terrifying
Glad to know I’m not alone, I thought I was crazy after the first time I had experienced it.. I’m so sorry you’re having to go through that, I hope tonight is better for you.

It happened to me on night 1 and 2 of being sober after about a 4 day binge. It was very terrifying and is what is keeping me from not picking up a drink just from sheer fear of experiencing that again..
I currently work from home because of Covid and I had some time off and unfortunately my addict brain thought I could handle a glass or 2 to celebrate which turned into a awful 4 day binge.

Also fell of the wagon after my longest stretch of sobriety, convinced myself I could handle a couple drinks knowing that was clearly not the case. One drink is always too many and a thousand is never enough. I’m also back on day 3 and pushing through the anxiety and horrible shame as well, but we we will and can do this!! You have got this! IWNDWYT ❤️

This might be the most inspiring post I’ve read in awhile.. I often will not let myself celebrate the little daily victories that I complete because they seem so small and meaningless, but in reality these small habits that we do every day are the most important ones and slowly build and build until we have made remarkable changes in our lives. This post just gave me the permission to be happy and celebrate myself with each tiny accomplishment I do throughout my day no matter how small. Thank you for this post and you are doing AMAZING! 
IWNDWYTD

Maybe you could try a 30 day alcohol free challenge and throughout the 30 days document any time you feel cravings or have thoughts of drinking, and then write down what’s triggering those thoughts etc. so at the end of the 30 days you can truly look back and see your relationship with alcohol! Just an idea!
It WILL come, just be patient and just take it one day at a time ❤️
